result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B's article grid really does work: prose sits in a min(65ch, 100%) middle column, while pre, tables and figures span the full 1120px. It also handles scrolling tables and long unbroken strings well. A says code breaks out to --wide, but its CSS keeps a pre inside .prose capped at the 68ch measure, and its 1360px frame token adds little beyond the 1120px wide cap. B is weaker on over-engineering: its 4/8/12 column tokens and .grid class go unused, and the feature row hard-codes 12 columns. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Answer A's breakout is built into the CSS. A three-track article grid keeps prose at 65ch, while pre and table-wrap span the full 1120px width and scroll inside their own box. It uses three breakpoints and one shared frame, though it hardcodes repeat(12) in .feature instead of using its --cols token. Answer B gives sound tokens and a useful testing checklist, but its usage example says a pre inside .prose 'breaks out to --wide', and the CSS doesn't do that. It also adds a separate 1360px frame cap and a fourth breakpoint that the pages don't clearly need.
